objective.question: Why does the measured nonlocal banded Jacobian stabilize the first electron step but fail to reduce later-step Gummel work?
objective.promotion_target: O(10) average FP/step with short-horizon parity before long-horizon qualification

frozen_invariants: plasma equations and converged fixed-point equations

hypotheses.statement: The normalized electron-potential Jacobian shape W=diag(VTe/ne) dn_e/dphi changes materially from electron step 1 to later steps, so a static Gen13 banded matrix becomes stale even after state rescaling.
hypotheses.test: Direct 20x20 central-difference basis Jacobians at converged control states t1, t2 and t3, with identical delta_phi=1e-4 V.
observables: relative Frobenius delta W(t1)->W(t2), W(t2)->W(t3), W(t1)->W(t3)
hypotheses.guard: This lane diagnoses the electron map only and does not modify Gummel relaxation.

hypotheses.statement: The qualified outer Picard relaxation alpha=2/(1+chi_e) is too small for the Gen15 band5-preconditioned operator and masks possible acceleration.
hypotheses.test: Keep the Gen15 band5 matrix, placement and state scaling fixed; vary only outer relaxation alpha in {0.02,0.05,0.10,0.20}.
hypotheses.guard: A faster but parity-invalid or unstable setting is not promotable.

decision_logic: Large W-shape drift with little relaxation benefit supports adaptive/recomputed Jacobian work.
Small W-shape drift with strong relaxation benefit supports retuning the outer iteration around the static banded operator.
Both effects present supports an adaptive Jacobian plus adaptive relaxation design.
Neither effect present falsifies both leading Gen16 explanations and requires iteration-matrix/placement analysis.
